speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the examination room. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; have you noticed any cyanosis, grunting, or retractions since birth? Additionally, what are the results of your initial maternal history and prenatal screening? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The mother had gestational diabetes. No other significant family or prenatal history. Social history: Not applicable

speaker: Patient
text: The cyanosis improves with oxygen administration. No feeding difficulties were noted prior to onset of symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual initial assessment for respiratory distress; a urinary tract infection typically does not present with cyanosis or retractions. Since the cyanosis improves with oxygen, please have the parents describe the newborn's feeding behavior and whether they are producing any urine. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis AND Urine_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to surfactant deficiency. The normal urinalysis rules out the suggested urinary tract infection, and the clinical presentation of cyanosis improving with oxygen, combined with the newborn status, is most consistent with RDS. I am requesting a chest X-ray to confirm the characteristic "ground-glass" appearance and assess for pneumothorax. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray
